```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">COVID-19 Academic Impact in Illinois

Damian Betebenner &amp; Adam Van Iwaarden
Center for Assessment

July 26, 2021</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/02.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">How do we quantify academic impact using test data
• The pandemic was like a “headwind” that (presumably) slowed down the
learning of students due to a variety of factors.
• Headwinds impact progress in two ways.
• They decrease the rate of progress (i.e., decrease student growth).
• They decrease the distance travelled (i.e., decrease attainment).
• We can use test data in two ways to quantify the impact of this headwind:
• Best way: Quantify how much the rate of learning (i.e., growth) slowed:
• IAR: Use historical skip-year growth norms to quantify growth and compare to pre-COVID
growth.
• Next best way: Look at how much 2021 status changed:
• ILEARN: Use 2019 status (or some adjustment thereof) as a proxy.
• NOTE: When providing 2021 data, users will (correctly) want to compare
their data to 2019 (or 2020 with ACCESS). The task is to make sure that
such a comparison is an apples-to-apples comparison.
Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Illinois 2</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Results
• Overall academic impact was large in both ELA and mathematics.
• Recovery associated with large impacts will likely take multiple years and
require additional supports beyond just normal schooling (right-size the
intervention)
• Both status-based analyses as well as growth-based analyses support these
findings.
• The following tables illustrate numerically what these impacts were.
• For rough comparison, the effect size impacts we are seeing for
achievement are roughly 1 to 5 times as large as what were reported for
Hurricane Katrina in Louisiana depending upon grade and content area.
(Effect sizes of -0.06 and -0.17 are associated with Katrina).
• Groups experiencing minimal impact should be scrutinized closely with
regard to pre-pandemic level of educational efficacy.
Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Illinois 3</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/06.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Performance by initial level of achievement
• We are beginning to look at impact by demographic subgroup
(coming shortly) as well as impact by academic subgroup.
• We examined academic impact by the prior academic achievement
(low versus high achieving using prior scale score decile).
• To dig deeper we regularly look at SGP distributions by prior score
decile. For cohort referenced SGPs we expect a uniform distribution.
For baseline referenced SGPs, deviations from uniform indicate
impact.

Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Illinois 6</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/15.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">School level impact
• We are currently in the process of finalizing school level impact
analyses and want to share some of the initial looks at these results.
• To calculate impact at the school level we calculate for each school:
Unadjusted Impact = Median SGP2019- Median SGP2021
• We adjust for regression to the mean for this difference score by
using pre-pandemic (2017 to 2019) school level median SGP scores.
• Results forthcoming shortly

Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Illinois 7</div>
```
